FR-001.title: The player interface MUST provide a responsive layout for viewport sizes from 1024×600 through 2560×1440 at 100% browser zoom.

FR-002.title: Every player presentation state MUST fit within the browser viewport without horizontal or vertical browser-page scrolling when populated with representative content.

FR-003.title: The terminal header, active content region, and available navigation controls MUST remain simultaneously visible at every supported desktop viewport.

FR-004.title: Responsive changes MUST prevent interface text and controls from overlapping, being clipped, or extending outside the viewport.

FR-005.title: The hacking state MUST keep the board data, attempts, activity log, input preview, and available interactions visible and usable at every supported desktop viewport.

FR-006.title: Text size and spacing MUST adapt across the supported desktop range while keeping primary terminal text at least 16 pixels at 100% zoom.

FR-007.title: The terminal frame and decorative presentation MUST remain wholly contained within the viewport without reducing the usable content region below what the active state requires.

FR-008.title: Content that exceeds the available content region MUST use localized overflow without causing browser-page scrolling or hiding the terminal header or available navigation controls.

FR-009.title: Long or unbroken authored values MUST remain fully accessible without widening the browser page or covering another control.

FR-010.title: At 200% browser zoom, all information and controls MUST remain reachable and usable without overlap or content loss, although localized scrolling MAY be used.

FR-011.title: Keyboard focus MUST remain visible whenever a player moves among interactive terminal controls.

FR-012.title: Responsive presentation changes MUST preserve existing connection, navigation, hacking, reveal, and audio behavior.

decisions.decision: Interpret no scrolling as no browser-page scrolling while allowing bounded local overflow for exceptional authored content and enlarged views.
decisions.why: The interface must stay fully visible while arbitrary user-authored content has no finite maximum length.
decisions.rejected: Clipping or shrinking unbounded content below a readable size.

decisions.decision: Remove the maximum viewport scale cap and reflow the hacking view at enlarged effective widths.
decisions.why: Players must retain browser zoom and reach every state at 200% enlargement.

decisions.decision: Detect hacking fit from actual descendant bounds as well as scroll extents.
decisions.why: overflow:hidden can report equal scroll and client extents while child rows are visibly displaced outside their allocated columns.
decisions.rejected: Treating scroll-extent equality alone as proof that every required region fits.

decisions.decision: Use a conditional tight stacked geometry that removes compact gaps and preserves the columns natural height.
decisions.why: The exact dense-history case needs a few pixels of reclaimed spacing while FR-015 forbids shrinking hacking text and FR-016 forbids scrolling or pagination.
decisions.rejected: Reducing the hacking font or paginating/clipping the board or activity log.

decisions.decision: Fit every hacking row through one rendered CSS variable using a base-to-failure binary search with a 0.25 CSS-pixel interval.
decisions.why: Actual column width, 16-row height, fallback glyph metrics, and required-region containment can impose different maxima; rendered measurement satisfies all bounds and the 0.5-pixel acceptance tolerance.
decisions.rejected: A viewport-only formula or unbounded width fill that could clip rows or starve the activity log.

decisions.decision: Choose compact/stacked/tight geometry before row-font fitting and observe only the stable terminal body size.
decisions.why: This keeps layout orientation deterministic and recalculates on render, resize, and font readiness without observing font-sized descendants.
decisions.rejected: Observing the hacking rows or columns themselves, which could create a resize feedback loop.
